Shared CDCAtlas review standards

Source: REVIEWING.md

These standards apply to ChatGPT and Claude, within the user’s permissions. Read AGENTS.md. A review is an assessment of a defined change, not automatic permission to edit, publish, approve or merge.

Policy revision and coverage

For PRs, fetch AGENTS.md and REVIEWING.md from the actual target branch at its recorded current base SHA. Record both policy paths and that SHA. Proposed policy changes do not govern their own review. If retrieval fails, disclose the gap; do not claim the policy was read. For local reviews, use committed policy at HEAD and assess uncommitted policy edits separately. Implementation uses applicable working-branch and subdirectory guidance.

Identify the copy, branch, exact commit, target, comparison scope and policy revision. GitHub reviews exclude unpushed changes. Use the merge base for the initial PR diff. Read changed human-written code and relevant surrounding paths; trace effects through callers, joins, returned objects, tests, documentation and affected workflows. Reserve whole-package coverage claims for whole-package reviews.

On follow-up reviews, inspect changes since the last reviewed revision, retaining relevant full-PR context. Account for changed bases and rewritten history. Revisit unresolved findings only with new material evidence; do not repeat resolved findings. For generated-only changes, check agreement with source, exports and imports and keep the report proportionate.

Development-aware judgment

Identify the stated milestone and intended behavior before judging it. Distinguish: - Verified defects introduced or exposed by the change. - Validation or evidence gaps, without calling uncertainty a proven defect. - Methodological decisions requiring an explicit rationale or user decision. - Intentional unfinished work within a documented development milestone. - Unrelated existing limitations and future release-readiness work.

Prioritize silent corruption, incorrect calculations, broken installation or exports, misleading claims, and privacy violations. Intentional documented interface changes can be acceptable during development; accidental breakage remains a defect. An incomplete milestone is not automatically release-ready. Do not demand unrelated cleanup. When alternatives are reasonable, present their tradeoffs and a recommendation; consider an argument with a recommended default when it serves plausible user needs. Follow AGENTS.md’s decision process rather than rejecting options categorically or requiring them for every close choice. Evaluate tests and CI independently: passing assertions can encode an incorrect scientific assumption. Explain whether external findings are agreed with, partly agreed with or disagreed with, and why.

Scientific and service checks

Verify affected behavior against current authoritative CDC documentation and available metadata. Start with CDC’s AtlasPlus overview and documentation links, the application’s current Technical Notes, Glossary and FAQs, and metadata for the actual request. Historical extracts require their matching historical documentation, not silently substituted current definitions. For ACS use the requested year’s table metadata/universe and Census geography-vintage documentation. These are starting points, not evidence that every package mapping is correct. Use an available authorized browser/web-fetch or other retrieval tool; shell network access is not required. Disclose unavailable sources and the resulting evidence gap rather than inventing verification.

Check, where affected: - Indicator definition, unit, population, denominator, age universe, geography and reporting period. Distinguish diagnoses, prevalence, deaths, counts, rates and percentages; names such as cases or rate100000 do not prove the underlying unit. - Suppressed, unavailable, missing and true zero values. Never silently turn suppression or missingness into zero. Check primary/complementary suppression and indicator-specific rules without reconstructing hidden values. Existing explicit zero sensitivity options are assumptions, not observed zeros. - Character geographic identifiers and leading zeros, geographic level, boundary changes, ACS vintage and crosswalk completeness. - Overlapping strata, total rows versus subgroups, whether quantities are additive, uniqueness of keys, join cardinality and duplicated observations. - Request filters and payload codes; splitting, batching or pagination where applicable; completeness across responses; schema changes, timeouts, malformed/empty/partial responses and error handling. Do not assume this endpoint has pagination merely because other APIs do. - Returned indicator, geography, year and subgroup against the request, including unexpected or silently omitted cells. - Source revisions, retrieval dates, cached-response age, and limitations of reverse-engineered endpoints. HTTP success alone proves none of the above.

For modeled county-to-tract/block-group or other allocation, distinguish estimates from observed CDC values. Document assumptions and their rationale, verify denominator compatibility and trace unknown categories, filtered counties, no-county remainders, empty strata and unallocated rows. Check totals within the appropriate indicator/year/geography/stratum, while separately checking distribution and coverage. Matching a national total or preserving county sums does not validate subgroup or geographic estimates. Do not invent definitions or silently choose unresolved methodological defaults. Preserve authoritative sources, versions/dates when available, and durable rationale near the code or in existing scientific documentation; link from PRs. The issue/vignette map in AGENTS.md supplies project rationale, not independent verification of CDC definitions.

Validation

Choose validation scope for each PR from the changed behavior and its downstream reach, not merely the number of changed lines. State the selected scope and rationale. Run focused checks first; expand when shared interfaces, scientific calculations, dependencies, or observed failures warrant it. Distinguish failures introduced by the PR from existing failures. When attributing a failure to the PR, compare with the target-branch baseline under equivalent conditions where feasible; otherwise state that attribution remains uncertain. If adequate validation is unavailable, report the specific gap. Do not expand into an unrelated whole-package audit.

Relevant CI results from the exact reviewed revision may supply validation evidence; independently assess whether those tests check the intended behavior. Use focused local execution for gaps, suspected defects and independent synthetic examples, keeping observed CI distinct from personally executed checks.

Inspect test fixtures, helpers, startup and load-time effects before execution. Use only the isolated, permitted environment described in AGENTS.md. Inspect expectations independently of implementation; favor hand-checkable synthetic cases and regression failures before fixes. Mock at service boundaries, retaining meaningful parsing, arithmetic and join checks. Consider missing rows, NA versus zero, unknown codes, duplicate keys, incompatible denominators, mixed indicators and partial geographic coverage. Use numerical tolerances appropriate to the calculation, not arbitrary rounding to force agreement.

Keep these evidence categories separate: 1. Source inspection and mathematical reasoning. 2. Personally executed synthetic checks. 3. Recorded public-response checks (with provenance/retrieval date). 4. Live public-API checks (request, retrieval date, cache status, scope). 5. Observed CI results (revision and job). 6. Author-reported checks, not independently reproduced.

Never present synthetic checks as proof of live compatibility. Live checks must respect the suppression and data boundaries in AGENTS.md. Do not execute live checks blindly: inspect the existing imputation pipeline against those boundaries before selecting checks. The full live suite is appropriate only when every selected path is permitted; otherwise report the subset and coverage gap. Distinguish modeled estimates with assumptions and uncertainty from recovering suppressed observed counts. Report OS, R/package versions if execution occurred, failures, skipped checks and material coverage limits. Give exact remaining maintainer commands, including vignette rebuilds when affected, only after stating prerequisites, network/cache effects and what the commands establish. Check dependency minimums and material Windows portability risks. Generated documentation can be a staged follow-up if explicitly documented, but broken exports/imports or installation are substantive defects.

Reporting

Lead with the change’s purpose and scoped conclusion. Group actionable findings as Must fix, Should fix or Consider, omitting empty groups. For each, give source path/line, evidence, failure mode or uncertainty, practical consequence and suggested resolution. Keep methodological questions distinct from verified defects. Avoid stylistic nitpicks and unrelated backlog items. Explain any pre-existing issue that the change materially worsens.

State actual checks, policy revision and material limitations. A clean scoped review means no actionable findings in the inspected scope, not comprehensive correctness, formal approval or release readiness. Silence or a skipped/failed automated review is not approval. Self-review is not independent review.
